public_rationale: On 2024-07-28, Marcus wrote that LLMs cannot be counted on and that this is part of why Fortune 500 companies lost confidence in them after the hype. One part holds. Lucidworks ran a survey in April-May 2024, which The Register reported on 2024-06-12. It found that 63% of firms planned to raise AI spending, down from 93% in 2023 (e2). The survey gave several reasons for the slowdown. Worries about the accuracy of AI responses were up fivefold. Cost worries were up 14-fold, and financial returns were weak (e1). The other part is not borne out. In a report dated 2024-03-21, a16z said dozens of Fortune 500 and top enterprise leaders it spoke with were nearly tripling their generative AI budgets and moving work into production (e3). The same report named hallucination and safety as one of two primary concerns. That concern made firms more cautious about customer-facing uses (e4). Together, the evidence shows cooler spending plans, with accuracy as one of several named reasons. It does not show Fortune 500 firms as a group losing confidence in LLMs. It also does not show that reliability weighed more than cost or returns.
limitations: The Lucidworks sample is 1,000 firms with 100 or more employees across 14 industries, not the Fortune 500.
The primary Lucidworks report could not be read. Its findings are cited through The Register.
a16z is a venture firm, and this report is written for AI founders. It does not say how the interviewees were chosen.
These surveys cannot measure how much of any cooling was caused by reliability.
The source text says 'a bit part'. This record reads that as 'a big part'.
OpenAI's claim that 92% of Fortune 500 companies use its products (e5) dates from August 2024, after the period. It measures use, not confidence.

from_speaker: these systems simply cannot be counted on
Fortune 500 companies have lost confidence in LLMs
our_interpretation: Plain reading: by July 2024, large companies (Fortune 500) as a group had grown less confident in LLMs than during the 2023 hype, and unreliability or inaccuracy was a major stated reason.
Target period: from the start of the 2023 hype to the post date (2023-01 to 2024-07-28).
Surveys of big-company leaders count as evidence, even when not limited strictly to Fortune 500 firms. A narrower sample is noted as a limitation.
criteria.support_condition: Surveys or reports from the period show large enterprises cutting back, slowing, or growing more sceptical about LLMs, with accuracy or reliability named as a major reason.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Surveys or reports from the period show Fortune 500 or similar large firms increasing LLM budgets and deployments with growing confidence, or show reliability was not a major reason for any cooling.
